rows.30:0c6c:
Heh heh heh... Quite something, to say that about yourself.
Either you're terribly sure of yourself, or you really are kind.
Well, never mind.
One look in your eyes will tell me which it is.{p}
rows.30:111c:
The make-up class went like this: they were handed a worksheet, and whoever solved the problems on it could go home.
There were quite a few hard problems on it.
They weren't the kind you could solve easily.
And they were the sort of students who end up in make-up classes in the first place, you know.
Not exactly the type who love to study.
So they scribbled down any old answers and went to show them to the teacher.
Then they got the teacher's go-ahead and hurried off home.
I suppose the teacher understood how it was, too.
Well, it was a make-up class in name only.
But he was different.
He sat down to the worksheet in earnest.
He wasn't the kind of person who breaks a promise.
Even if it's only a promise to a teacher, once you've made it, you have to keep it, don't you?
Just like you, really.
So he stayed behind alone in the classroom, trying to solve it to the very end.
Problems he couldn't find so much as a hint for, however hard he thought.
"What, you're still here?
I forgot all about you. You can go home now, {a}."
The teacher had been sure everyone had already gone home.
The classroom light was on, so the teacher looked in, suspicious, and found one student still there.
Awful, isn't it?
Well, since the teacher had given permission, he got ready to go home, and when he happened to look around, it had already gone completely dark.{p}
rows.30:25a8:
He felt sweat break out all over his body.
...What's wrong?
Isn't that sweat on your face?
This isn't about you, you know.
This is the story of the other {a}.{p}Will you turn around?
rows.30:2de0:
What?
What did you just say?{p}Say that once more for me.
rows.30:2e58:
I hope I didn't hear you wrong...
Did you just say you'd run away and leave an injured girl all alone?
That's what you said, isn't it?
You just told me yourself that you were kind.
Am I wrong?
Or have my ears gone funny?
I'm sure I heard you say it.
You're kind, aren't you.
So go on, help her.
I absolutely hate being lied to.
When someone lies to me, it makes me want to kill them.
Understand?
If you lie again, I'll kill you.
Don't you dare lie.{p}
rows.30:302c:
You're kind, after all.
So you will help her.{p}
rows.30:306c:
"Are you okay?
I'll carry you on my back."
You gently helped her up and carried her on your back.
And she said:
"...Thank you.
...Don't let go of me."
You're kind, after all.{p}You know how you answered her, don't you?
rows.30:3ca0:
"...This hallway is so long, isn't it?
...I wonder when this hallway will ever end.
Was there ever a hallway this long at school...?"
Her voice, spoken to no one in particular, melted away into the darkness.
"...It's awfully cold, isn't it?"{p}
rows.30:55d0:
Day after day, mosquito after mosquito landed on his arm.
It made her feel awful.
She couldn't even speak to {a}, and yet those mosquitoes...
She brooded over it until she even came to think that if she could drink {a}'s blood, she wouldn't mind being swatted dead like a mosquito.
Kitajima was terrified of herself for feeling that way.
So she decided to confess to {a}.
She gathered every ounce of courage and decided to tell him how she felt.{p}...How will you answer her?
rows.30:5878:
The next day, the two of you decided to eat lunch together on the roof.
A boxed lunch, eaten together with her...
She looked so happy.
A happy time went on for a while.
But...{p}
rows.30:5ac0:
And her behavior escalated more and more.
She simply could not forgive the mosquitoes for sucking your blood.
{a} is mine.
And yet the mosquitoes are still sucking {a}'s blood...
Whenever she thought about it, she was beside herself.
She couldn't forgive the mosquitoes that drank your blood, but she also grew unable to forgive you, for letting them drink it so easily.
And she became even more violent toward you than before.
When you scolded her for it, she burst into tears.{p}
rows.30:6360:
...I feel sorry for Kitajima.
I'm sure she was led astray by whoever owns that voice.
I don't think the mosquito swarms were her curse.
It must have been something in this school...
that led her astray, I believe.
{a}.
If a girl who fell for you heard that voice, what would you do?
I wonder if you could break the curse of that voice's owner...
That's the end of my story.
Whose turn is it next?{p}
rows.30:64e4:
Why would you have to turn her down?
She was so very sweet and modest.
So {a} was overjoyed when she confessed to him.
And he decided to go out with her.
Listen.
You knew nothing of the terrible feelings that had taken root in her heart.{p}
